name: X6100
subtitle: Field reference
kicker: Independent reference. Not a Xiegu publication and not affiliated with Xiegu.
verified: Compiled from the Xiegu X6100 Operation Manual, September 2026. Not checked against a radio. Stock firmware only. The manual documents no repeater operation.
specs: 10 W on SSB, CW and FM. 2.5 W AM carrier
5 W on SSB, CW and FM. 1.5 W AM carrier. The supply halves it
Yes. Matches to about 4.5 to 1, first tune within 15 s
3000 mAh at 12 V. About six hours to charge
USB Type-C, with the port driver installed
keys: Opens the digital function menu: noise reduction, blanker and notch.
A row under the screen that does whatever the display shows above each one.
Multi-function knob. Long press about a second to unlock.
Rotate for volume. Press once for squelch depth, again for RF gain.
Tap brings the tuner in line. Hold about a second starts tuning.
Long press about a second locks the panel.
quick: AGC knee, slope and hang. TX POWER. Mic selection and gain. Line levels. Monitor level. PTT mode. Band stack. Charger on or off.
RIT, XIT, split, and the IQ output.
Spectrum and waterfall averaging and reference, and backlight level.
Save the VFO, tag it, mark it, erase it.
Key type, speed, iambic mode, sidetone frequency and level, break-in time, dot to dash ratio, and a CW trainer.
Noise reduction and depth, blanker with width and level, and a digital notch with centre and width.
filters: Three selectable filters, shaped by a high cut and a low cut, with a default that restores them. Xiegu prints no bandwidth figures.
tasks: General settings, memory setting, save VFO. Name it with the tag item.
V/M switches VFO and memory. The left and right rockers step channels.
General settings, memory setting, erase memo.
General settings, radio setting 1, TX power.
Short press ATU to bring it in line, long press about a second to tune.
Rotate the multi-function knob to factory reset, press it, confirm. The radio shuts down and needs turning on again. Xiegu does not say whether memory channels survive, so photograph them first.
notes: Ten watts needs external power. On the internal pack it makes five, and the radio does not announce the change.
There is no receive scan on this radio. The only sweep it has is a standing wave sweep.
The control software wants the radio selected as an X108G, which is not obvious and costs people an evening.
Everything on this card is stock firmware. Third-party firmware changes the keys, the menus and the labels, and none of it is in Xiegu's documentation.
Xiegu's manual describes no repeater offset, shift, tone or tone squelch for this radio. It has FM but no documented repeater support, so nothing about working a repeater appears on this card.
control: The CH342 port driver must be installed before anything sees the radio
Select the radio model as X108G in the control software
